title.narrative: IOM - Strengthening women's resilience as peace actors in Nord and Sahel 2022-25
IOM - Stärka kvinnors motståndskraft som fredsaktörer i Nord och Sahel 2022-2025

description.narrative: Insatsen ämnar stärka kvinnors rolls som fredsaktörer genom att stärka deras kapaciteter, deras socioekonomiska egenmakt och deras deltagande i lokal dialog.

Since January 2016, Burkina Faso has been facing a deteriorating security situation marked by the proliferation of armed violence. The violence has led to massive internal displacement, with 1,850,293 registered internally displaced persons (IDP) as of 31 March 2022 (CONASUR). This amounts to almost 10 % of the total population of Burkina Faso. The security situation and the resulting displacement of people have led to a humanitarian crisis marked by closed schools and health centers as well as widespread food insecurity. The displacement of people strains the social cohesion of communities as IDPs and host communities have to share, and sometimes compete for, resources that were already limited before the crisis. The Nord and Sahel region of Burkina Faso find themselves at the epicenter of this crisis. The two regions contain 43 % of all registered IDPs in Burkina Faso which, in combination with pre-existent and widespread poverty exacerbates the vulnerabilities of the population and weakens their resilience. Women represent the majority of IDPs (53 %) and are particularly affected by the crisis since they are to a greater degree exposed to sexual violence, discrimination, forced marriage, slavery, and other human rights abuses. In addition, they bear a disproportionate burden in providing for their households and their children. At the same time, due to systematic exclusion, they lack the necessary access to resources and decision-making to effectively participate in the promotion of peace and social cohesion within the communities.The proposed intervention aims strengthen women's (IDPs/Host communities) resilience and thus enable them to contribute significantly to the consolidation of peace and the strengthening of social cohesion in the North and Sahel regions. This will be achieved by improving their inclusion in local planning processes and community dialogues as well as strengthening their socio-economic autonomy through income-generating activities (IGA) and improved infrastructure.
It aims to strengthen the role of women as peace actors by enhancing their capacities, their socio-economic empowerment and their participation in local dialogue.

The overall objective of the proposed intervention is that:
Women (IDPs/Hosts) will be more resilient and will be able to contribute significantly to the consolidation of peace and the strengthening of social cohesion in the North and Sahel regions
This will be achieved by working towards the following results and outputs:
1. Women actively participate in local planning processes and community dialogue on peace and social cohesion in the North and Sahel regions
1.1 the capacities of local government and services are strengthened in the promotion of gender equallity, and mechanisms for the socio-economic inclusion of vulnerable people (IDPs) are reinforced
1.2 Women's leadership in targeted communities is promoted and women act as promoters of peace and protection of vulnerable communities
2. Socio-economic empowerment of women (IDPs/Hosts) is enhanced in the North and Sahel regions through sustainable sources of income
2.1 Women's committees (IDPs/Hosts) improve their socio-economic autonomy and have strengthened capacities in income-generating activities
2.2 Successful initiatives by beneficaries (IDPs/Hosts) are disseminated nationwide

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Key Results
Overall, positive changes during the intervention period based on findings from the final evaluation that can be highlighted include:
- Increased perception of women's role in peacebuilding (from 84.9% to 98.4%). - Improvement in peaceful coexistence in intervention communities (from 67.7% to 82.4%). - Women who feel that their economic empowerment and wellbeing has improved (from 48.9% to 72.7%).
Areas with little or no positive change include:
- Female beneficiaries participating in peacebuilding initiatives (from 56.7% to 58.1%). - Women involved in a conflict prevention or management process (35.6% to 29.8%).
Example of results specifically in relation to the two outcomes are presented below:
Outcome 1: Women actively participate in local planning processes and community dialogue on peace and social cohesion in the North and Sahel regions
Trainings on conflict sensitive approach, gender and the role of women in the consolidation of peace and social cohesion: 90 municipal administrative authorities and heads of decentralized and technical services and 77 community and religious leaders were trained. According to the perception study, 80% of trained administrative authorities and 70% of community and religious leaders said that they have a better (good or very good) knowledge of gender promotion as well as mechanisms for the protection and socioeconomic inclusion of vulnerable people, including IDPs. According to community leaders, "awareness raising and training on conflict management, tolerance, and living together have allowed communities to better understand the importance of peace and collaboration ." Officials of the technical services involved in the implementation of the project think that "The project has fostered understanding between host communities and internally displaced people, which has helped to reduce intercommunity tensions."
Community consultations: A total of 162 people, including 46 women, participated in the community consultation sessions in the two regions. This approach allowed for a transparent and inclusive implementation of the project's activities while minimizing the risks of tension and exclusion. According to the final evaluation report, more than 85% of the beneficiaries said they had been involved in the preparation and implementation of the project.
Strengthening women's coordination groups, trainings to strengthen women's knowledge and capacity in themes related to gender, gender based violence, protection and women's leadership and the organisation of committees and consultations with the purpose to enhance community dialogue, and advocacy, for the promotion of the role of women in inclusive local governance, decision-making processes, as well as support for social cohesion, conflict resolution and peace initiatives. According to the project's final evaluation, 22.9% of women beneficiaries reported becoming active leaders.
Outcome 2: Socioeconomic empowerment of women (IDPs/Hosts) is enhanced in the North and Sahel regions through sustainable sources of income
Income generating activities (IGA) were created in order to strengthen the socioeconomic situation of women. The process to set up the activities included: identification of the economic niches and promising professions in the two target regions selection of partners for setting up income generating activities and training and equipping beneficiaries.
In total, 850 beneficiaries, including 724 women and 385 IDPs, have been trained in the various areas of technical skills and provided with individual and collective kits for the realization of their IGAs. Out of the 850 IGAs, 94% were still functional during the latest data collection in the field at the end of the activity period. The percentage of women who felt that their economic empowerment and wellbeing had improved had increased from 48.9% at the beginning of the project to 72.7% at the end of the project. The same was true for the percentage of women who say that their income has improved, which increased from 50.1% to 68.4% over the same period.
To help disseminate the most successful initiatives, the project set up seven incubators in areas such as fish farming, poultry farming, weaving and livestock feed production. These incubators provided a framework for continuous learning and reinforcement for the beneficiaries, as well as for other segments of the population.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
